Consult with your attorney to assess whether the offer adequately compensates you for your injuries, medical expenses, lost wages, future medical needs, pain and suffering, and any other relevant damages. Consider your long-term needs and the financial security that an accepted settlement might provide. 2. Understand the Risks of Trial: Going to trial carries inherent risks. While your cousin may be correct that juries can be sympathetic, there is no guarantee of a favorable outcome. Trials are unpredictable, and the decision will ultimately be in the hands of the jury, who will consider the facts, evidence, and the arguments presented by both sides. The verdict could result in a higher award than the settlement, but it could also be lower or result in no award at all. 3. Weigh the potential benefits of a higher jury award against the time and resources you would need to invest in preparing for trial. 4. Assess the Strength of Your Case: Evaluate the strength of your evidence, witness testimonies, and legal arguments.
